Description

CB2 is the cannabinoid receptor of immune cells, and its presence on sensory neurons is still debated, although mouse genetics points to a role in nociceptors. Activated by endocannabinoids, CB2 signals through Gi to inhibit adenylate cyclase. In rat models of OA, CB2 agonists reduce pain and spinal sensitisation, but in human hand OA cannabidiol did not reduce pain.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is blue: CB2 relieves pathological pain.

The whole blockblueCB2 relieves pathological pain
A CB2 agonist attenuates OA pain and spinal neuron responses, and a G protein biased one gives lasting analgesia. One CB2 agonist sensitised OA joint afferents through TRPV1 (Schuelert 2010).
